title: Cellular Respiration
seo_title: Cellular Respiration Worksheets: Glycolysis, Krebs Cycle, ATP and Fermentation (Biology)
standard_text: Use a model to illustrate that cellular respiration is a chemical process whereby the bonds of food molecules and oxygen molecules are broken and the bonds in new compounds are formed resulting in a net transfer of energy.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on cellular respiration (NGSS HS-LS1-7): the equation, glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain, ATP and fermentation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Bonds in glucose and oxygen break, new bonds form in CO2 and water, and energy moves to ATP.
body_html:
How to think about it

Food + oxygen → CO2 + water + usable energy (ATP).

C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy (ATP)

  • Glycolysis (cytoplasm) → Krebs cycle (matrix) → electron transport chain (inner membrane).
  • With oxygen: about 36 ATP per glucose. Without oxygen (fermentation): 2 ATP.
Example

5 glucose broken down completely. CO2 released?

6 per glucose

6 × 5

Answer: 30

Example

10 glucose by fermentation. ATP?

2 per glucose

2 × 10

Answer: 20

Common mistakes

  • Thinking respiration means breathing.
  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Thinking energy is created. It is transferred.
  • Thinking fermentation makes more ATP. It makes far less.

faq.q: What is the equation for cellular respiration?

faq.a: Glycolysis in the cytoplasm, the Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix and the electron transport chain on the inner membrane.
It happens without oxygen and makes only 2 ATP per glucose, with lactic acid or alcohol and CO2 as products.
